context_requirements: AR-dependent transcriptional program (e.g., prostate lineage or AR-transfected context)
DHT or other androgen present to compete with antagonist
AR pathway addiction for proliferation/survival to see downstream transcriptional consequences
falsifiers: No decrease in AR-dependent genes or proliferation genes in VCAP at 24 h
Strong transcriptional response in AR-negative lines (PC3, A375, A549, HA1E, HCC515, HT29) comparable to VCAP
Clear AR-dependent transcriptional changes at 6 h in all lines
No difference in response between VCAP and AR-negative lines

evidence.supports: p,p'-DDE inhibits androgen binding to AR and androgen-induced transcriptional activity
procymidone acts as an AR antagonist inhibiting DHT-induced transcriptional activation
enzalutamide resistance in AR-positive prostate cancer lines involves AR pathway and non-AR pathway gene expression changes
AR antagonist bicalutamide inhibits prostate cancer cell proliferation and AR-regulated gene expression
androgen blockade derepresses retroelements and stimulates interferon signaling in prostate cancer

changes: Removed HMGCS1 and HMGCR from late_up: these are sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis genes, not established AR-antagonist-induced genes; their upregulation is not supported by the cited mechanism.
Changed HEPG2 line_response from weak to none: HEPG2 is AR-negative and not an AR-dependent prostate lineage line, so a transcriptional response to an AR antagonist is not expected.
Kept MCF7 as weak: MCF7 expresses AR and can show limited AR-dependent transcriptional changes, but is not AR-addicted for proliferation.
Kept VCAP as strong: VCAP is AR-positive and AR-pathway-dependent, consistent with the strongest response among the listed lines.
Kept PC3 as none: PC3 is AR-negative and should not respond to an AR antagonist.

Kept kinetics slow and magnitude weak at 6 h / moderate at 24 h: AR-antagonist effects on transcription are indirect and require turnover of AR-dependent transcripts, so early effects are expected to be weak.
Kept generic_effects proliferation_down and g1_arrest: these are appropriate generic consequences of AR antagonism in AR-dependent lines.
Kept evidence PMIDs 7791873, 10188193, 27036029, 17218635, 35584120: each abstract supports the stated claim about AR antagonism, resistance, or downstream signaling.
